blocks.html: Opportunity Cost is the potential benefit or value lost when one alternative is chosen over another in business decision-making.

Opportunity Cost helps businesses evaluate trade-offs when making decisions about time, money, and resources. Every choice has an associated cost in terms of what is foregone by not selecting the next best alternative. It is widely used in strategic planning, budgeting, and resource allocation.
Opportunity cost is not always a direct financial expense but represents the value of the next best option not chosen. It is considered when:

items.html: Investing in one project over another

blocks.html: Businesses use it to ensure resources are used in the most efficient way.
A company chooses to invest in paid ads instead of content marketing. The opportunity cost is the potential long-term organic traffic and leads that content marketing could have generated.
Opportunity Cost is a key concept in business decision-making that highlights the value of alternatives not chosen. Understanding it helps organizations make smarter, more strategic choices.
